title: Multi-KB Federation: Namespace Isolation for Team Knowledge
summary: Multiple knowledge bases can be combined under a single MCP server with namespace prefixes. Each namespace has independent search, index, and health resources.

content.overview: Federation allows a single MCP server to expose multiple knowledge bases under namespace prefixes. An agent connected to one server can search across auth-team KB, infra-team KB, and frontend-team KB without switching connections. Each namespace maintains isolation — same module ID in different namespaces won't collide.
content.examples:
Set up federation:
1. Have multiple KB directories (e.g. team-auth-kb/, team-infra-kb/)
2. In the main KB's config.json, add federation.namespaces entries
3. Run km serve — namespaces are auto-loaded
4. Agent calls federated_search('JWT', namespaces='auth,infra') to search across both
content.references: See storage.py:load_federation() for the namespace loading logic. See mcp_server.py:create_server() for the federation resource registration. See cache.py:ModuleCache._make_key() for namespace-prefixed keys.
content.caveats: Namespaces are loaded at server startup and cached in memory. If a namespace KB is updated (via git pull or module changes), the MCP server needs to be restarted to pick up changes. Federation only works with local file paths — remote KBs must be cloned first. The current implementation does not support recursive federation (a namespace KB cannot itself have federation namespaces).
